question.text: Chandragupta Capital is cross-checking the DCF value of investee Ananya Pharma using trading comps. Ananya's FY25 PAT = INR 25 crore; Shares outstanding = 50 lakh. Listed peer-set mean P/E = 22x. The AIF applies a 20% DLOM (Discount for Lack of Marketability) for Ananya being unlisted. What is the DLOM-adjusted value per share?

explanation.text: The Logic: EPS = 25,00,00,000 / 50,00,000 = INR 50. Unadjusted price = 22 x 50 = INR 1,100. Applying 20% DLOM: 1,100 x (1 - 0.20) = INR 880. A discount to the quoted market ratio is applied to reflect illiquidity when valuing an unlisted company using listed-peer P/E. The Trap: INR 1,100 ignores DLOM entirely. INR 1,320 adds a 20% premium instead of deducting a discount. INR 704 applies an excessive 36% discount (e.g., double-discounting). Note: The illiquidity discount may be lower if a near-term exit is expected, but it is conceptually required whenever a listed-peer multiple is applied to an unlisted investee.
